name: Ocean Jasper
physical: Traditionally linked to a calm, refreshed feeling
Associated with relaxation after long days
Often kept nearby for comfort during stress
summary: Ocean Jasper is the orbicular, bubbly-patterned chalcedony from Madagascar, loved as a stone of joy, calm and emotional renewal.
intro: Ocean jasper is a type of orbicular chalcedony found only on the coast of northwestern Madagascar, in a few sites accessible at low tide. It forms round, eye-like orbs and swirls in a wild palette: sea green, cream, pink, tan, grey, white and sometimes blue-grey. Cut and polished, the patterns resemble rippling waves or a bed of tiny bubbles, which is how it got its name. It can be a sort of chalcedony with druzy pockets of tiny quartz crystals. Beautiful, relatively scarce and often sold in beads, cabochons and slabs, it is among the most distinctive jaspers.
history: Ocean jasper was discovered in the early 2000s in Madagascar and quickly gained fame among collectors and crystal lovers. The most celebrated deposits sit on the shoreline, where tides expose the rock twice a day, so mining is limited and the stone may be harder to harvest in some seasons. Some of the original sites have been exhausted or closed, and more recent finds appear under names like sea jasper. Because supply is limited, quality pieces with strong patterns carry premium prices. Cutters value the stone for the way each slice looks like a different aquatic scene, a kind of abstract underwater painting.
meaning: Ocean jasper is called the stone of joy in crystal practice. Healers link it to the heart and throat chakras and use it to lift the mood, ease stress and encourage playful self-expression. People who feel stuck in negative thoughts sometimes keep it nearby to remember that moods flow like waves. It is said to soften self-criticism and bring acceptance of past mistakes. Many practitioners tie it to healing of old emotional hurts and a renewal of hope. The orbicular bubbles are read as symbols of release, as if worries float off to the surface. It is a gentle, uplifting stone for sensitive people who want light, not heavy, support.
howToUse: Wear ocean jasper as a pendant or bracelet to keep a bright mood close. Place a polished piece on your desk, bath edge or bedside to create a calm corner. Hold a stone in meditation and imagine waves washing over you and carrying away tension. Carry a small tumbled piece in a pocket for days that feel heavy. Combine it with aquamarine or blue lace agate to deepen a sea-themed ritual. Set a sphere in a living room for relaxed gatherings.
care: Ocean jasper is relatively hard and tolerates water. Rinse in lukewarm water and dry it with a soft cloth. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or a rest on selenite. It is fine in sun or moon. Pieces with druzy pockets are more delicate, so avoid scratching or hard knocks. Store separately from harder gems and avoid ultrasonic cleaners, which can loosen small crystals.
identify: Real ocean jasper has varied, irregular orbs with natural color blends, some drusy pockets and a fine polish. Imitations use dyed jasper, resin or painted stones with repeating, too-perfect circles. Genuine stones come from Madagascar, so a seller who cannot name the origin is suspicious. Check the underside for flat paint or glue. If the colors look neon, assume dye. Ocean jasper can be confused with orbicular jasper from other locations.

faq.q: What is ocean jasper good for?
faq.a: Ocean jasper is used for joy, calm and emotional renewal. Crystal healers link it to the heart and throat chakras and keep it nearby when they want a lighter mood and gentler self-talk.

faq.q: Where does ocean jasper come from?
faq.a: True ocean jasper comes from a small stretch of coastline in northwestern Madagascar, where tides expose the rock. Because supply is limited, genuine material with strong patterns can be pricey.
It is an orbicular chalcedony, closely related to jasper, and the trade calls it ocean jasper. It often includes agate and drusy quartz pockets, so it is a mix of microcrystalline quartz forms.
